intended_object: The unit section of the identity component G° of a group scheme G over a one-point base S. This is the unique S-morphism e° : S → G° whose composite with the inclusion G° ↪ G is the unit section e : S → G of G. It is the "one" of G° viewed as a group scheme (Milne, Algebraic Groups, Prop. 1.34). Inferred from the docstring and from its use as `one` in `Scheme.identityComponent_grpObj`.
explanation:
The definition takes the S-morphism η[G] : 𝟙_(Over S) ⟶ G, whose underlying scheme map is S → G. It factors that map through the open immersion `(Scheme.identityComponent G).ι` using `IsOpenImmersion.lift`. The range condition holds because S has a single point, so the image of the unit lies in the connected component of η(s₀). The compatibility with the structure maps to S follows from `lift_fac` and `η[G].w`.

The companion lemma `identityComponentOne_comp_ι` shows that composing with the inclusion gives back η[G]. Since the inclusion is a monomorphism, this property determines the morphism uniquely, so it is exactly the restricted unit section of G°.

On generality: the hypotheses (one-point nonempty base, locally connected underlying space) come from how the file defines the identity component itself, as a topological connected component that is open. Over a general base the identity component is defined differently, through the fibres, so this setting is needed by the construction here and is not an artificial restriction of this definition.

Mathlib has no corresponding declaration for identity components of group schemes. The definition is also a genuine mathematical object, namely the unit of the subgroup scheme G°, not just an implementation device.
